summary: Cyllene is an Arcadian mountain nymph in Greek mythology, named by Pseudo-Apollodorus as a consort of Pelasgus and, in one variant, the mother of Lycaon. She must be distinguished from Cyllen, the male eponym of Mount Cyllene, son of Elatus.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: In Bibliotheca 3.8.1 Apollodorus reports that Pelasgus begat Lycaon either by Meliboea, daughter of Ocean, or by a nymph named Cyllene.
Mount Cyllene in Arcadia is also named for the hero Cyllen, son of Elatus, and is famed as the birthplace of Hermes; the feminine nymph and the masculine eponym are distinct figures.
